rules.title: Mandatory Path Aliases
rules.description: Never use deep, fragile relative imports like ../../../.
rules.rule: Always use project-configured path aliases (e.g., @/..., @components/..., @utils/..., @hooks/..., @services/...).
rules.badExample: import { Button } from "../../../../components/common/Button";
rules.goodExample: import { Button } from "@/components/common/Button";

rules.title: Strict 3-Way File Separation (UI, Logic, Styles)
rules.description: Components must strictly isolate visual presentation, stateful logic, and styling into distinct files.
rules.rule: For every component: 1) <Component>.styles.ts contains styles only. 2) use<Component>.ts contains state, hooks, handlers, and side effects. 3) <Component>.tsx contains pure UI markup consuming the logic hook and styles.
rules.badExample: // Single 400-line file containing useState, useEffect, API calls, inline styles, and JSX markup all together
rules.goodExample: // Component.styles.ts (styles) + useComponent.ts (logic hook) + Component.tsx (pure UI view consuming hook and styles)

rules.title: Zero Inline Styles
rules.description: Never use style={{ ... }} in JSX or TSX.
rules.rule: Extract all styling to dedicated *.styles.ts files using SxProps, Theme tokens, or StyleSheet.create.
rules.badExample: Title
rules.goodExample: export const containerSx = (theme: Theme): SxProps => ({ display: "flex", color: theme.palette.primary.main });

rules.title: Mandatory i18n Translation Keys
rules.description: Zero hardcoded user-facing strings anywhere in the codebase.
rules.rule: All UI text, buttons, placeholders, dialog titles, errors, and toast messages must use translation keys via t("domain.key").
rules.badExample:
<Button>Submit Application</Button>
const errorMsg = "Failed to save user";

rules.title: Centralized API Endpoints
rules.description: Never write raw URL strings in components or services.
rules.rule: All endpoints must be declared in core/endpoints.ts under domain namespaces.
rules.badExample: axios.get("/api/v1/user/profile")
rules.goodExample: axiosInstance.get(ENDPOINTS.user.profile)

rules.title: Zero Direct Axios / Fetch in UI Components
rules.description: Components must never import axios directly or make raw network calls.
rules.rule: All networking must pass through domain API services (e.g. from @/apis or @/services).
rules.badExample:
import axios from 'axios';
// inside component: axios.post('/api/...', data);
rules.goodExample:
import { updateUserProfile } from '@/apis/user';
// inside hook: await updateUserProfile(data);

rules.title: Centralized RTL/LTR Theming
rules.description: Never hardcode dir="rtl" or dir="ltr" on components.
rules.rule: Direction is managed globally by root CacheProvider (stylis-plugin-rtl) and ThemeProvider.
rules.badExample: <Card dir="ltr"><Box sx={{ direction: "rtl" }}>...</Box></Card>
rules.goodExample: <Card><Box>...</Box></Card>

rules.title: Mandatory CSS Logical Properties
rules.description: Use bi-directional logical properties instead of physical left/right properties.
rules.rule: Use marginInlineStart, marginInlineEnd, paddingInlineStart, paddingInlineEnd (or marginStart/marginEnd in React Native) for full RTL/LTR compatibility.
rules.badExample: const boxSx = { marginLeft: 16, paddingRight: 8 };
rules.goodExample: const boxSx = { marginInlineStart: 16, paddingInlineEnd: 8 };

rules.title: Zero Emojis & Static Icon Glyphs
rules.description: No emojis or hardcoded icon glyphs in UI, code, comments, commits, or docs.
rules.rule: Render icons through the project icon component with a semantic name.
rules.badExample: <Text>Booking confirmed ✅</Text>
rules.goodExample: <Icon name="check-circle" /><Text>{t("booking.confirmed")}</Text>

rules.title: Zero Gradients & Invented Colors
rules.description: Colors must be traceable to the design system, never chosen ad hoc.
rules.rule: Use theme tokens only. No hex/rgb()/rgba() literals, no linear-gradient, no self-picked palettes.
rules.badExample: background: "linear-gradient(135deg, #667eea, #764ba2)"
rules.goodExample: backgroundColor: theme.palette.primary.main

rules.title: Zero Raw Color Literals
rules.description: Colors must come from the design system, never from a literal in a component.
rules.rule: Reference a theme token. Only the theme/tokens layer may hold hex, rgb() or rgba() values.
rules.badExample: <Box sx={{ color: "#0092BE", background: "rgba(0,0,0,.08)" }} />
rules.goodExample: <Box sx={{ color: theme.palette.primary.main, background: alpha(theme.palette.common.black, 0.08) }} />

rules.title: No Boilerplate Comments / Explain Complex Intent Only
rules.description: Never write obvious comments narrating standard code or component creation.
rules.rule: No comments for component creation, imports, state declarations, renders, handlers, or standard syntax. Only add comments for complex, non-obvious, or tricky business/algorithmic logic, using simple, clear explanations.
rules.goodExample: // Exness API requires epoch timestamps in milliseconds; convert before request payload (see partner doc #312).

rules.title: Zero Console Logs in Production Code
rules.description: Do not leave debugging console statements in production codebase.
rules.rule: Strip console.log, console.debug, and console.info before staging/production or route through a configured logger service.
rules.badExample: console.log("User data fetched:", data);
rules.goodExample: logger.debug("User data fetched", { userId: data.id });

rules.title: Zero Explicit any Types
rules.description: Never widen a type to any to silence the compiler.
rules.rule: Declare a strict interface or DTO. Use unknown plus a narrowing guard when the shape is genuinely unknown.
rules.badExample: const handle = (payload: any) => payload.id;
rules.goodExample:
interface Payload { id: string }
const handle = (payload: Payload) => payload.id;

rules.title: No Markdown File Sprawl
rules.description: Every change should not spawn a new summary document.
rules.rule: Extend the documentation that already exists. Create a new .md file only when explicitly requested.
rules.badExample: CHANGES_SUMMARY.md, IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md, FIX_REPORT.md added alongside the code change
rules.goodExample: A section appended to the existing README or standards document

rules.title: Delete Dead Code
rules.description: Unreachable code, unused exports, and orphaned files are removed in the same change.
rules.rule: Run the AST orphan finder and remove imports/variables/exports your change orphaned.
rules.badExample: Legacy function kept "just in case", wrapped in a commented-out block
rules.goodExample: Dead branch deleted; git history is the archive

rules.title: Reuse On Second Use
rules.description: Anything needed in two or more files belongs in the shared layer.
rules.rule: The second consumer triggers extraction into a shared component, hook, or utility -- never a copy-paste.
rules.badExample: The same status badge JSX duplicated across three screens
rules.goodExample: components/shared/StatusBadge.tsx consumed by all three screens

rules.title: 3-Layer Backend Architecture
rules.description: Enforce strict separation between Controller, Service, and Repository.
rules.rule: Controllers handle HTTP req/res -> Services handle pure business logic -> Repositories handle DB.
rules.badExample: // Controller querying DB directly with SQL/Mongoose logic inside req handler
rules.goodExample: class UserController { async getProfile(req, res) { const user = await this.userService.getUser(req.user.id); res.json(user); } }

rules.title: Offline-First SQLite Architecture
rules.description: Use fast embedded SQLite for instant zero-latency local operations.
rules.rule: Store user data in op-sqlite with an action queue for background syncing with the REST backend.
rules.badExample: Fetching data over network on every screen focus without local persistence
rules.goodExample: Query local SQLite table first, render UI instantly, trigger background sync in parallel.

rules.title: Multi-Provider AI Architecture
rules.description: Abstract LLM providers with automatic fallback and failover.
rules.rule: Implement an AIProvider interface for Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, and Groq with fallback orchestration.
rules.badExample: Direct hardcoded single SDK calls with no retry or provider failover
rules.goodExample: AIService trying primary provider (Gemini) -> fallback (Claude) -> secondary fallback (OpenAI)
